To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CACO models can achieve state of the art results in document classification on related language pairs with low resource settings.

(1) CACO can be trained with only 10 labeled examples per class in the target language and outperforms the state-of-the-art cross-lingual classification model in the low-resource setting, (2) CACO achieves competitive results in high-resource settings with only 10,000 labeled examples, and (3) CACO models can be further improved with a multi-task objective.
CACO is an effective framework to exploit cross-lingual character similarities for document classification, and that the multi-task objective can further improve CACO.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) How can we exploit cross-lingual similarities between related languages for document classification?
the problem of document classification with limited training data in a low-resource language.
the problem of text classification in the context of low-resource language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CACO model trained under a low-resource setting can rival cross-linguistic word embedding models trained in a high-resource setting.
our proposed model outperforms the state-of-the-art models in cross-lingual classification task.
CACO models are competitive with other state-of-the-art methods on related language pairs and are particularly effective in low-resource settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CACO is a simple yet effective framework that can be applied to any document classification problem with limited training data in the target language.
CACO is able to achieve comparable performance to cross-lingual embedding models, but requires much less training data.
CACO is a simple and effective transfer learning framework for low-resource text classification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
subword similarity is an important factor to consider when building cross-lingual models for document classification.
cross-lingual transfer can be achieved without relying on word-level parallel corpora, and the transfer learning framework is effective in low-resource settings.
cross-lingual transfer can be successfully achieved by exploiting cross-lingual similarities in written forms.
